Thanks for the issue! If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

issue.title: chore(travis): Test on Node 5, don't update npm in newer Nodes
issue.body:
Node 5 includes npm 3 by default so we don't have to update npm to make sure
it works on that version. On the other hand, most people don't upgrade npm
and just use the default included version, especially that it's very hard
to update npm on Windows. It's good to make sure Karma still works with npm 2,
especially that Node 4, current LTS will never upgrade to npm 3.

body: Ahh.. you are correct. I didn't notice that. Hmm. In that case I think the rule is behaving correctly. @eslint/eslint-team

The idea here was that there should be no space directly after a paren to which this code adheres. On the other hand, most people prefer to put a space between a comment and code wherever it lies in the file. So IMO either it behaves incorrectly or it needs more options.
@mzgol Was this working in the previous version of ESLint?
We can probably call this a bug. It's a bit of a gray area since now we're (correctly) ignoring comments in this rule, so it looks like the space is right next to the paren when we do the check.
